# E119 -- WeWork Brand Guidelines

## Metadata
- **Brand:** WeWork (Coworking / Workspace)
- **Year:** 2018 (creation date)
- **Source PDF:** 9df237dffb858485de7cab07001516e6.pdf
- **Pages:** 30
- **Produced by:** Not credited (Adobe InDesign CC 13.1, landscape 1008x648 format)

## Brand Strategy
- Design system called "FrameWork" -- a visual metaphor for WeWork as a living framework
- Creative values: Fresh, Timeless, Understated, Inviting, Fun
- Artistic edge with commercial pop; innovative but inclusive
- Three core brand principles:
  1. **Intentional** -- Utilitarian, Under-designed, Honest
  2. **Flexible** -- Nimble, Responsive, Scalable
  3. **Human** -- Warm, Inclusive, Real
- "We build structures that build community" -- not just spaces but schedules, events, networks, connections

## Logo
- Treated as a sign-off; should be the last thing read on any execution
- Positioned at bottom right of English-language pages (end of natural read order)
- In multi-canvas/scrolling executions, logo may repeat but never visible twice on same canvas
- Clear space rules defined
- Don'ts: no effects (outlines, shadows, gradients), no stretching, no containers/shapes, no rotation (except exterior building signs), no placement first in read order, no multiple logos on same canvas, no graphic elements in clear space, no busy backgrounds

## Typography
- **Primary:** Apercu Pro Medium -- modern sans-serif with classical cues; contemporary, refined, functional but characterful
- **Secondary:** Apercu WeWork Mono Regular -- used for informational data (dates, times, locations)
- **Type hierarchy (5 levels):**
  - Display: Title case, one grid unit high, leading 97%, optical kerning
  - Headline: Title case, 40% of Display, leading 108%
  - Subhead: Title case, 60% of Headline, leading 116%
  - Copy Large: Sentence case, 50% of Subhead, leading 133%
  - Copy Small: Sentence case, 70% of Copy Large, leading 133%
- **System alternatives:** Email: Helvetica Medium + Courier Regular; Google Suite: Karla Bold + Roboto Mono
- Don'ts: no altering proportions, no mixing cases, no mixing weights/new styles

## Color Palette
- **Primary (foundation):** Black (#2B2B33, PMS Black C) and White -- constant through time
- **Secondary palette** with levels/sets for specific usage scenarios:
  - Dark Blue: #1D4D68 / PMS 7477C
  - Blue: #006BA0 / PMS 307C
  - Orange: #F99C1C / PMS 1375C
  - Yellow: #FCD200 / PMS 109C
  - Dark Green: #007055 / PMS 568C
  - Green: #00965D / PMS 340C
  - Dark Red: #CC0E1D / PMS 186C
  - Red/Coral: #F05253 / PMS 178C
- Rules: white always an option for background; flood colors for commercial print/digital only (not in-office); single color per execution; no colored text on black backgrounds; no colored ink on colored stock

## Graphic Elements
- Design system "FrameWork" can flex from functional to expressive, rigid to loose, quiet to loud
- Framework metaphor: structure that supports community
- Minimalist approach -- "do more with less"
- No specific pattern or illustration system mentioned

## Photography
- **Spaces:** Airy, light, clean, symmetrical/linear, energetic, pops of color, natural lighting
- **People & Moments:** Authentic, candid, creation/collaboration/connection; never stock or contrived
- **Events:** Both wide shots and intimate human moments
- Bright, natural light or studio light used naturally
- Symmetrical composition preferred to show architectural intention
- Workspaces shown in use but somewhat stylized and decluttered
- **Video:** Real, not overly produced; diegetic lighting; energetic editing; music with guitar/piano/strings/drums

## Applications
- Not extensively shown in this document; focused on system elements
- Covers advertising, OOH, digital assets (TV, App, Website), in-office printed materials
- Templates with specific color usage specifications

## Tone of Voice
- **Professional but Chill** -- key positioning
- **Human** -- warmth, personality, purpose in every communication
- Voice modulates based on content and context
- Key attributes maintained from operational signage to global ad campaigns
- Inclusive, never niche or exclusive

## Outliers & Unique Elements
- Logo treated purely as a sign-off (always last in read order) is an unusual and distinctive approach
- The "FrameWork" naming of the design system as a brand metaphor is clever
- Relatively concise at 30 pages but covers strategy, elements, and voice
- Secondary colors organized into "levels" with specific usage parameters by scenario
- Video guidelines included with specific music instrument recommendations

## Quality Score
3 / 5
Well-articulated brand strategy and principles, with good typography and color systems. However, the document is relatively brief, lacks detailed layout/grid guidance, has minimal application examples, and the graphic/pattern system is underdeveloped. Strong on voice and photography direction.
